portion_doctrine: Segment 31 is primarily Reddit UI boilerplate, navigation, ads, and comment thread scaffolding with minimal actionable content. The real content consists of curated photography contract best practices derived from r/photography and r/WeddingPhotography community recommendations.
operating_rules: Never do paid photo work without a contract
Use a lawyer to draft or review contracts rather than relying solely on templates
Hire a lawyer if you plan on doing many more weddings
Keep design minimal and professional - black and white with minimal design preferred over decorative versions
Use PDFs instead of Word documents for contracts; PDFs preserve formatting
Start with a reputable template or CRM as baseline (Pixieset, HoneyBook, 17hats, Studio Ninja)
Tailor contract to your jurisdiction and services - laws vary by state/country
Review contracts periodically as laws and business practices change
Deposit should be non-refundable if event is canceled before a certain date
named_methods: Limitation of Liability and Indemnity clauses - limit damages to fees paid, include force majeure/acts of God clauses
Replacement/Backup Photographer Clause - permit an associate if you cannot perform
Clear Scope of Services - spell out dates, start/end times, locations, number of edited images, delivery method, turnaround time
Payment & Deposit Terms - include deposit amount, refundability, payment schedule, cancellation policy
Usage/Copyright/Model Release - state who retains copyright and how images may be used
Deliverables and Client Responsibilities - clarify meals, second shooters, extra fees, termination conditions
numbers: Coverage includes eight hours, beginning at 2 PM
specific_tactics: Specify meal coverage: include clause stating if photography session is more than 4 hours long, client is responsible for feeding photographer and team
Use digital workflows - PDFs with Fill & Sign tools rather than Word documents
Include force majeure/acts of God clauses to protect against unforeseen circumstances
Have photographer cancellation clause specify return of all fees to clients
Exclude willful misconduct or gross negligence from indemnity provisions
Clarify scope with videographer vs photographer distinction for multi-shooter scenarios
tools: PDF readers with Fill & Sign functionality
gates: Legal review recommended before signing - many advise hiring a lawyer
Avoid contracts with overbroad indemnity that excludes willful misconduct or gross negligence carve-outs
Question non-disparagement or review restriction clauses - may violate Consumer Review Fairness Act
Be cautious of exclusivity fees for other photographers - clarify scope
contradictions: One expert recommends Calibri font for simplicity/professionalism; another expert recommends serif fonts (like EB Garamond) for extended text readability, calling Calibri 'MS Word's default' as reason to avoid it
weird_gold: EB Garamond typography specification: 12 pt font, 15 pt line spacing, 10 pt inter-paragraph spacing, 1.7 inch margins on letter paper, aiming for 45-90 characters per line (sweet spot: 70)
Line spacing formula: should be 120% of point size, no bigger than 145% (e.g., 12 pt font = 15-17 pt spacing)
After-paragraph spacing: 50-100% of text point size
